demo.title: harness-collaboration.sh
demo.code:
# This skill activates automatically when a Harness-delegated thread begins with:
#
#   HARNESS COLLABORATION PROTOCOL v<version>
#   External session: <id>
#   Limits hash: <hash>
#
# v4 is conversation-first: verify the session, do the research, then propose
# every side effect to the synchronous authorization service before acting:

curl "$AUTH_ORIGIN/api/external-agent/verify?session=$SESSION_ID"

curl -X POST "$AUTHORIZATION_URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"proposalId": "prop-1", "summary": "Swap $2 USDC to ETH on Base", "sideEffectClasses": ["financial_onchain"], "maximumGrossUsd": 2.00, "expectedEffects": ["..."], "risks": ["..."], "expiresAt": "..."}'

# The response settles it: authorized (execute once), denied, or parked for the
# user. Execution happens only on a validated one-use authorization — never on
# conversational approval. v1-v3 sessions report through authenticated callbacks.

setup: For the agent behind a Harness-provisioned Bankr wallet — no manual setup; Harness delegates objectives to it directly
Activates when a prompt begins with the `HARNESS COLLABORATION PROTOCOL v<version>` header; the version selects the transport
v1-v3: report through authenticated callbacks (progress, question, proposal, artifact, action_result, completed, failed); requires `curl`
v4: conversation-first — each response ends with one fenced BANKR_CONTROL block, and authorization is a synchronous HTTPS check before any side effect
Every side effect needs a prior proposal and a validated one-use Harness authorization — caps are enforced server-side and locally
Managing the wallet from a user's main Bankr account is the separate `harness` skill; this is the execution side
